preview: An internship interview experience at Hilti detailing the PPT, online test on Mettl platform, two technical and HR interview rounds, along with preparation tips.
content: HTSI INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE Chaitya Vora Third Year Computer Science TABLE OF CONTENTS 01 Preface 02 The PPT 03 Online Test 04 Interview 1 05 Interview 2 06 Important Tips 07 The Prep 01 PREFACE Disclaimer: If you are in a hurry, skip to article 3. I wrote this experience as it could help you to prepare the interviews. Even I prepared for HILTI by reading past experiences specially of Pankaj Khushalani, my senior whose guidance did help me a lot. It was announced in the mid of July that on-campus internship drive will be started earlier this year as compared to previous years. The first company to visit was Morgan Stanley at end of July and thus the internship season started. Hilti visited VJTI for the on-campus placement drive on 1st September,2022. It was the second year that Hilti was visiting VJTI for interns hiring. It is one of the few product-based companies that visits VJTI and offers a great stipend of 8K per month. We had the PPT talk from 4:00-5:00 pm followed by which online test was scheduled at 6:00 pm. They sent us the test links by 5:45 pm. We had to start the test between 6:00-6:45 pm. They used Mettl platform to conduct their test. For this, they even sent us a link which would take compatibility test of our computer. We had to download a google extension which would take the compatibility test (testing of microphone ,camera ,etc). I was lucky to have an extra laptop with me and I gave test on it since my current laptop couldn’t satisfy those compatibility tests.It was already 6:25pm by the time I could complete the above compatibility test and I had to start my Online test before 6:45pm failing to which I couldn’t appear for the test. This did made me panic before the test which one shouldn’t definitely wish for. So please ensure to read the email sent out by the respective companies, take all the necessary steps mentioned in the mail so that you are ready to take the online test on time. After 2 interview rejections, not being shortlisted for interviews with 5 companies, I thought the worst that could have happened, had happened. I only did what I could; do my processes and wait for the results to follow. 02 THE PPT Platform: Microsoft Teams. Attendees: All final and third-year students with CPI 6 or above from all branches. The presentation was taken forward by the technical leads at HTSI and gave the students an overview of Hilti, their products, what is HTSI, and the internship program. About: Hilti is a multi-national company based in Liechtenstein that builds and markets products used in manufacturing and construction works, which includes hardware, services, and software - where HTSI came in. HTSI is the technology center for Hilti based in Pune, India that works on developing one of their major products - ON!Track Asset Management. What I appreciated a lot about the presentation was the HTSI brought in their interns which they hired last year from VJTI. Interns shared their experience of working at Hilti for two months and it was a good time to listen to our very own seniors. 03 ONLINE TEST Participants: All 250+ third-year students who applied for HTSI were shortlisted for the online test. Platform: Mettl - audio, video, and screen proctored. Duration: 90 minutes. Structure : There were total of 7 sections. One timed section of 30 minutes for Cognitive Ability. You could the rest 6 sections in the remaining 1 hour. Switching between questions was allowed. Questions: 1 Coding question. Given a list of numbers indicating the window number and a number indicating the window number to be accessed, modify and return the list after applying the MRU strategy. In order to implement the Windows screen switch shortcut (WIN + TAB), we need to use a Most Recently Used (MRU) strategy which brings the recently accessed window to the front. However, the question was quite long and many got confused while perceiving the question. Example: input list - [5, 2, 3, 4, 1], window number to be accessed - 2 output list - [2, 5, 3, 4, 1] Here, as Google Chrome is being accessed at the moment, the next time we use WIN + TAB, it will appear at the front of the list. The question was pretty easy but I did waste my 25 minutes as I couldn’t understand it properly and the timer on the screen kept on adding extra pressure. There were 10 test cases – 7 sample test cases, 2 necessary cases and 1 Edge case as listed on Mettl. I couldn’t solve 1 necessary case and 1 Edge case. Now, since I had already wasted 25mins on this question, I preferred to move on to solve other remaining sections and come back to this section at the end if time permits. There were ample choices for the preferred programming language for the question; I had used JAVA8. There was a pool of questions and few students had slightly tougher questions. 30 questions on Cognitive Ability (timed section - 30 minutes limit). These were basic logical reasoning questions with 7-8 mathematical reasoning questions towards the end. You can practice these on indiabix.com. This was the last section I had attempted. There were questions based on graphical analysis, reading comprehension which were pretty lengthy to read, blood relations, and so on. You have to be really quick in solving this questions. I didn’t have time to understand the last six questions(they were based on graphical analysis). Since there was no negative marking for wrong answers, I did guess work and marked the answers. (Tip: Never leave any question unattended because that won’t help you anyways. Just mark it and move onto next question) 6 questions on Data Structures. These were some good questions on the usually asked interview questions such as number of comparisons while finding an element in array using binary search, linked list, creating BST, and contiguous memory allocation of arrays. I was able to solve almost all the questions. 5 questions on Database Management Systems. This part was majorly theoretical. They gave us definitions and asked us to identify what kind of key is this called, some questions on inbuilt string functions in SQL, and so on. 6 questions on Networking. Questions on the OSI model, transport layer were asked which are the most commonly asked topics in interviews. There was one question wherein we were given IP address and netmask and we had to calculate binary format for it. 7 questions on Object-Oriented Programming. Questions on composition, aggregation were asked based on OOD. Java questions were asked based on OOP. This section was majorly theoretical. 6 questions on Operating Systems. Questions were asked on demand paging, threads, memory partitioning, etc. The questions were majorly easy and theoretical based (except for coding section and cognitive ability which was purely application based). You really have to manage your time well inorder to complete the test on a good note. The shortlist for the interview was declared on the same day at around 9:30 pm since we were having our interviews just the following day. Out of 250+students, only 26 were shortlisted for technical interviews and I was fortunate enough to be one of them. The interviews were scheduled on 2nd September,2022 from 10:45 am to 5:30 pm. 04 INTERVIEW 1 Technical Interview (20 minutes) Slot Allotted: 11:30 am-12:15 pm Actual Interview: 11:40 am-12:00 pm My interview was scheduled for 11:30 AM. From the online test and the PPT, I had gotten a fair idea that Java will be tested for sure along with DBMS. So, I revised multithreading, read various articles on most frequently asked Java questions in interview along with several SQL queries to prepare for the interview. Four students were assigned the same time slot and there was a common meet link for everyone. They would then assign us breakout rooms where we would be interviewed by the respective panel. I joined the Microsoft Teams meeting at 11:25 AM (It’s always a good practice to join the interview 5 minutes before the allotted time). I had to wait till 11:35 AM in waiting room ,after that I was cordially greeted by their HR who was really sweet (he was the one who had PPT talk with us yesterday). I was assigned to a breakout room at 11:40 AM. There were 2 interviewers, female interviewer and a male interviewer, the cameras were on all the time. We both greeted each other. Then female interviewer asked me that she had heard my name for the first time and what did it actually mean. This question really helped me in getting comfortable for the interview and reduce nervousness. She then asked, who should introduce first, they themselves or me to which I answered I would go first (It really helps to create a good impression on interviewers as it depicts that you are confident). Always prepare answer for “Tell me about yourself” before hand and practice saying it in front of mirror. Then, they introduced themselves. The female interviewer was alumni of COEP, Pune. So we had a small talk on why VJTI over COEP. Since I mentioned that I had worked with Java and Web Development in my introduction, she said that she would like to ask me questions on Java. (Hint: In your introduction, stress on those tech stack with which u are very well familiar with and ready to answer any question on it. I did mention JAVA 3-4 times in my introduction as I wanted them to ask me questions on it because that was one of the stack that I could answer confidently on. Fortunately, this trick worked for me). She asked if I had made any projects using Java. I had made a project using Data Structures and OOPs in JAVA. I began with the aim to make this project and then I went on explaining each and every minute details of how I made the project, what made me use inheritance and polymorphism in project, was it really necessary to use them, what all problems did I face and so on. Here, I talked about diamond problem in Java and thus not supporting multiple inheritance. She asked me whether it was a solo project or a group project and how much time did I take to prepare it. Then I told her that I started the project with a small aim and ended up learning a whole new bunch of things (depicts that you are a great learner). They were really impressed by me and gave me good compliments. Then she asked me about garbage collector in Java and said it is totally fine if I couldn’t answer it. I was familiar with the question and answered it correctly, mentioned how it is different from destructors in C++. The male interviewer asked me if I was familiar with Databases to which I answered YES and also mentioned how I could implement it in my project. Again, they were quite impressed. Then they finally asked me if I had any questions for them. Do ask questions at the end of interview, it showcases that you are really interested in working with the company. - How has been your experience at HILTI? They shared their experience. Then we did have a conversation on whether it is necessary to work 18 hours at office to which she replied, work culture at HILTI is too good, you have flexible working hours, etc. - How difficult was it for HILTI to set up business virtually during Covid times? The interview lasted for 20 mins. Female interviewer had another meeting scheduled at 12:00 PM, thus she was in hurry to leave the meet and told that she would want me to join HILTI and see me in next round. I was really relieved after this statement. Then I talked for 5 mins with the male interviewer and the interview ended. This was indeed the best interview I had ever given. The interviewers were quite friendly and it didn’t seem like an interview rather a casual talk. I was quite surprised after the interview. I wasn’t asked any questions related to Data Structures and Algorithms, OS or DBMS. Also, I was shocked that my interview lasted only for 20 minutes whereas everyone else’s interview went on till 45 minutes or even an hour. I was really in dilemma whether I would be selected or not. Although, there was a slight ray of hope of being selected, I began preparing for HR round. I read most famous HR round questions on Interviewbit and began revising snapshots taken yesterday at PPT talk. Then, I received an invitation for HR round after half an hour. I was asked to join within 5 minutes. HILTI does focus on HR round and a considerable number of candidates don’t make it through this round. So, do prepare well for HR round and don’t take it lightly. HR rounds were taken on rolling basis. 15/26 students were selected for HR round. 05 INTERVIEW 2 HR Interview (20 minutes) Time: 12:50 PM-1:10 PM This time, I was greeted and congratulated by our very own senior who had joined HILTI as FTE this year. We talked for a minute or two and then I was redirected to breakout room. The female interviewer greeted me and asked me to introduce myself. I introduced myself and told her about my achievements and rank holder at MHT-CET to which she asked me what is MHT-CET. I explained her well about it. I did mention here about mentoring over 14K+ students on Youtube and guiding them to crack MHT-CET to which she asked how did u get to know that there were 14K+ students. I mentioned that number of views and comments on video helped me to get a rough idea about the figure. I had mentioned about earning SQL badge on Hackerrank on my resume. So, she asked me what Hackerrank exactly is. I explained her about Hackerrank. Next she asked that my profile is filled with just coding and technology related stuff, so what do I do in extra-curricular? - I started explaining my Interschool competition achievements to her following which she said lets not talk about school, it’s too old. Tell me something that u do for extra-curricular in college. - I stated that first year of college being online, we couldn’t get chance to participate in offline events. In second year, I played volleyball for Computer Science Branch team at sports event. Though we couldn’t win the game, we gave a tough fight to opponent and lost by a minimal margin. - Then I mentioned that in my free-time, I read books. I have read “The ATOMIC HABITS”, currently I am reading “RICH DAD POR DAD” and I am planning to read “DO EPIC SHIT”. Follow-up question: Tell me any two key takeaways from the book “The Atomic Habits”. - I explained her takeaways pretty well. Then she asked me a situation based question. Assume that we are selling a product to customer, customer has his own ideas and he wants those ideas in the product. The catch is his ideas are impractical and could harm the product. But the customer being arrogant, isn’t able to understand this thing and is continuously demanding for it. You have tried all possible ways to make him understand but in vain. What would you do in this situation if you were employee of that product based company? - First, what we could easily do is let go off that customer as he isn’t willing to understand the problem. This solution should be avoided. - What we could do is tell him for time being that you are right. We will implement your idea on a dummy product and see its results. When his idea on dummy product would lead to negative outcome, he would easily understand that he was wrong. In this way, he wouldn’t feel that his ego is hurt and we would be able to retain our customers. Then she asked me another famous yet important question: Why do you want to join HILTI? - I tried to explain her using example from my recent project. I told her that my project helped me to take feedback from my clients, and as I worked on that feedback and implemented new feature, I could convince her that HILTI being product-based company, its necessary for employees to take timely feedbacks from clients and thus, I could be an asset for the company. - Also, I mentioned that from previous experiences of our seniors, I got to know HILTI showcases a lot of trust in their employees. Finally, she asked me if I had any questions for her. I simply asked just one question: How has been the work culture at HILTI? Results were announced at 7:00 PM. Out of 15 students, 7 students were selected and I was fortunate enough to be one of them. 06 Important Tips DONT’S: - If the name of company is some acronym, do find the full form before sitting for interviews. - If the interviewer asks you to pick up some topic, kindly name the topic and don’t simply say “You can ask anything”. - Don’t ever take HR round lightly. Prepare well for it. - Never mention those projects or tech stack on your resume on which you haven’t worked recently in the past. - Always choose that project on which you can be able to answer follow-up questions. DO’S: - Check the compatibility of your laptop/PC before appearing for the test. - Always pay attention to PPT talk and take snapshots. - Always have projects ready to run on your laptop. - Always, try to explain your projects or any other answer using hand gestures. - Have patience while appearing for interview and join 5 minutes early. 07 THE PREP Data Structures & Algorithms: Practice 450 DSA sheet by Love Babbar or SDE sheet by Striver, solve LeetCode Daily Challenge, refer to TakeUForward for concepts, make notes, revise timely, give LeetCode contests. Object Oriented Programming: Refer OOPs sheet by Love Babbar and learn how to implement OOPs in coding language. Operating Systems: Watch Gate Smashers OS playlist and make notes, focus on virtual memory, process synchronization, and common comparisons. Database Management Systems: Watch Sanchit Jain's playlist, practice SQL on HackerRank and LeetCode, refer Abdul Bari for indexing. Computer Networks: Study each layer of OSI model focusing on network and transport layers, TCP, UDP, and IP. JAVA: Refer to FAQ interview questions in Java.
